searches.note: Eighteen searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's; one (Cara Sur in Spanish) returned nothing relevant. Four were restricted to a house's own domain and are read as primary through their summaries: graffignawines.com, fincalasmoras.com twice, bodegascallia.com, pyroswines.com. Four blocked the author's own sources so that a second, independent source would show. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.

Where a detail rested only on an uncited critic or a single listing it was cut or softened; where the house's own sheet or a primary body corrected the record (Pyros's 2021 sheet, the Boletín Oficial for Resolution 30 of 2024) the record was set right with its source.

changed: wine.making: was 'about half of the wine was aged in oak barrels for around twelve months'; now part of the wine, about half by one listing, since the listings and reviews read give twelve months of oak for part of the wine but agree on no share.
wine.glass: was written from the oak note and the valley's style; now plum, blackberry, black pepper and liquorice from reviews of the 2007, 2012 and 2014 Centenario wines.
table: was 'half of it aged in oak'; now part of it, as above.

story: was the founder came 'as a boy' and 'pushed the railway on ... in 1885'; now as a youth (sources give twelve and sixteen) and followed the railway in the 1880s by the house's account, since the house's timeline does not tie the event clearly to 1885.
story: the museum's opening, November 2003, added from two San Juan sources.
story: was 'Late in 2018 ... agreed ... the sale closed in 2019'; now the sale announced in January 2019, the date of the San Juan press and the trade report; no source read confirmed the closing.

story, traps, cards: was 'the house moved its winemaking to the Uco Valley' in 2022; now the range turned towards Uco Valley fruit while keeping San Juan vineyards, since Forbes Argentina reports wines from Uco and from Cañada Honda in San Juan.
questions: the wine key now 'part aged about a year in oak'; the story stem now January 2019 and its explanation the press of that month.
sources: Taphunter (a listing) and the second Drinks Business page replaced by Tiempo de San Juan on the sale and Forbes Argentina on the Uco turn.
open: The founder's year of birth is not settled (arrival at twelve in one account, at sixteen in 1876 in another), so he stays described.
Whether the Centenario range is still made is not confirmed; listings run to the 2016 vintage.

changed: wine.making: 'fermented in temperature controlled stainless steel' cut, on one retailer's note only; the eighteen months in new French and American oak confirmed on the house's page.
story: the name's origin in the mulberry trees round the vineyards added, now on two guides (Grape Guru and Wine Folly).
story: was Decanter 'profiled the house as one shaking the status quo'; now carried a feature on the house, the page being a coverage feature, not an independent ranking.

others: Sagrado Pedernal was 'a Malbec ... at about 1,400 metres, the house's mountain wine'; now a red of the Pedernal Valley with cassis and eucalyptus, since the house's page gives neither grape nor height.
sources: the tasting note guide replaced by Grape Guru, the second source for 1993 and the Australian viticulturist.
open: One source gives 1992 for the founding against 1993 in most; 1993 kept.
Whether Gran Syrah is the house's flagship or one well known wine below Sagrado Pedernal and Mora Negra is the author's doubt and stands.

changed: wine.sites: was 'sandy loam to clay loam ... by its 2018 sheet'; now sandy loam by its sheets, the Magna sheet's soil line not being read in the summary and the house's other Tulum sheets giving sandy loam.
wine.glass: the clove, cinnamon and raspberry of an uncited review panel cut; the house's fig, cassis and vanilla kept.
story: was the Pie de Palo range 'to the north'; now between the Pie de Palo range and the Cerro Chico, the range lying north east of Caucete.
story: 'the house has bottled a Criolla too' cut, found in no source read.
others: Grand Callia was 'a red blend'; now a Tulum Valley red, since one listing calls it a blend of Syrah and Malbec and another a single variety.
open: One source gives 2001 for the founding against 2002 in most; 2002 kept.
The purchase of a Pulenta family cellar at Caucete in 2002, with a first wine in 2003, rests on Diario de Cuyo and is left out of the story.

changed: wine.making: was 'about twelve months in French oak barrels, only about a tenth new in the 2018 vintage by a review ... a further year in bottle by the importer's page'; now the house's 2021 sheet: about four weeks of maceration after fermentation, twelve months in mostly French and some American oak, about 15 per cent new, the rest second and third use, and nine months before release.
wine.sites and label: granite and schist cut (not on the house's sheet read), and the 2021 sheet's polygon of parts of parcels 3, 4 and 5 now stated; the label term no longer says single parcel.

wine.glass: was mint, liquorice and black tea from an uncited critic; now the house's note (deep violet, wild flowers, blueberry, blackberry) with Decanter's herbs, sour cherry, white pepper and flint.
wine.ageing: the critic's decade cut; now several years more by reviews.

story: 'the highest part of the valley' cut, a claim of rank on the house's word alone; 'mapped them closely' cut; 'a tenth new in 2018' now the 2021 sheet's second and third use barrels; Block No. 4 now 'a small part of it bottled alone'.
traps: Block No. 4 is now one block, not one parcel.
sources: the 2018 review replaced by Bonvivir, the second source for the purchase and planting of 2008 and the flint legend.
open: Whether Pyros and Callia's Pedernal estate are one vineyard is not settled; both are the Pon family's group.

changed: wine.sites: Paraje Hilario cut, found in no source read; the vines' age now some eighty years and more by importers' accounts (Brazos and the author's importer).

wine.making: was whole bunch in some vintages and seven months in concrete by one guide; now fermented spontaneously on its skins in ovoid concrete, mostly destemmed, without temperature control, by an importer's sheet, aged some months in concrete.
wine.label: the Paraje Hilario term cut, as above.

story: was the institute's 'decree' and 'the partners pressed for change'; now Resolution 30 of 16 August 2024, which added Criolla Chica or Listán Prieto to the list of varieties for quality wine as a red, by the Boletín Oficial; the pressing for change cut, found in no source read.

others: La Totora was 'vines planted in 1930 on alluvial soils of quartz'; now old vines near Barreal, part whole bunch, on its lees in a concrete egg, since one merchant gives 1930 to a different vineyard, Finca Maggio.
questions: the story explanation now names Resolution 30.
sources: the Boletín Oficial notice added as the primary source for the resolution; Bowler replaced by Brazos Wine, the second source for 2011, the two couples and the name.
open: The planting year of the oldest vines (1930 by one merchant, for Finca Maggio) is not settled and is left out.
The label form, Criolla Chica or Criolla, varies by vintage and source.

livingNamesNote: None is written in the fragment; the names are for the read-together agent to add to people.json, which this lane does not edit (Sebastian Zuccardi is listed already).

swaps.why: Graffigna is the historic house of San Juan, dated by its own page and the San Juan press to 1870, and the Centenario Malbec was a real San Juan labelled wine of the 2008 to 2016 vintages on many listings; the record now teaches it as such. The 2022 turn is towards Uco Valley fruit, not away from San Juan wholly (Forbes Argentina gives Cañada Honda fruit still), and Xumek rests on one wiki and one search, so it is not ready to replace a sourced record.

swapNote: The author's second doubt, Callia and Pyros in one family's group, is not a swap: the two are separate cellars and brands, in the Tulum and Pedernal valleys, and the plan rule forbids two picks of one producer, not two houses of one owner. Kept, and flagged for the read-together agent.
questions: All ten questions read: one key each, four options of one kind, the key never in the stem. Graffigna's wine key reworded to part in oak and its story stem moved to January 2019; Cara Sur's story explanation now names Resolution 30.
codexTension: The region summary calls the Tulum Valley at about 600 to 700 metres; Finca Las Moras gives 650 metres for its Tulum share, in agreement.
The region producers line calls Graffigna the province's best-known historic house, a judging word the flagship rules refuse; reported, not edited.
